name: Alert
abstract: Inline feedback block: a status glyph, a title, an optional explanation, optional actions and an optional dismissal.
discussion:
The glyph is part of the content, not decoration — it carries the same
meaning as the tone's colour, so the block still reads correctly when the
palette is monochrome or the reader cannot distinguish the hues.

Alert("Import failed", message: "The selected asset format is unsupported.", tone: .danger)

name: Badge
discussion:
Three variants trade emphasis against noise: `.soft` reads as a tinted chip
inside dense content, `.solid` as a single callout, `.outline` as a quiet
marker beside an already-bordered surface. Padding, glyph size and type
follow the shared `.controlSize` provider, so one badge definition serves a
dense table cell and a page header.

name: EmptyStateProminence
abstract: Explains why a region is empty and offers the one action that fixes it.
discussion:
An empty region without a next step is a dead end, so the recovery action is
part of the component rather than something every call site has to remember.
`prominence` covers the three places an empty state realistically appears:
inside a table body, in a full panel, and as a whole page.

name: ProgressCircle
discussion:
Reads better than a bar when the indicator sits in a square slot — a
toolbar, a table cell, a card corner — where a full-width track would look
arbitrary. Set `showsValue` to print the percentage in the middle; leave it
off when the number would crowd the ring at small diameters.

```swift
ProgressCircle(value: 0.72, diameter: 28, showsValue: true)
ProgressCircle(value: nil, diameter: 44)   // unknown duration
```

members.abstract: Ring thickness. `nil` scales with the diameter so the ring keeps the same visual weight at every size.

name: ProgressView
discussion:
Pass `nil` for `value` to switch to the indeterminate sweep, which is the
honest representation when the total work is unknown — a fake 30% that never
advances is worse than admitting the wait.

The sweep is driven by a clock owned by the node, so it starts and stops
with the view's lifetime and respects the system reduced-motion preference.

```swift
ProgressView(value: fractionComplete, tone: .success)
ProgressView(value: nil)   // unknown duration
```

name: Spinner
discussion:
The animation is registered with the owning node and cancelled when it
leaves the tree, so a spinner inside a conditionally-rendered branch never
keeps a clock running in the background. Reduced-motion is honoured by
freezing the glyph rather than hiding it — a static ring still communicates
"busy" without implying a percentage.

name: StatusTone
declaration: public enum StatusTone: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable
abstract: Semantic intent shared by CoveUI's feedback components.
discussion:
A tone is a meaning, not a colour. Components derive their ink, fill and
glyph from it, so re-theming — or shipping a monochrome theme — never has
to touch a call site.

members.name: color
members.abstract: The tone's primary ink: text, glyphs and outline borders.

members.name: icon
members.abstract: Glyph that carries the meaning without relying on hue, so the tone stays readable for colour-blind users and in monochrome themes.

members.name: ink
members.declaration: public func ink(onSolid theme: Theme) -> Color
members.abstract: Ink that stays legible on a surface filled solidly with `color`.
discussion:
Derived from the resolved colour's Rec. 709 relative luminance rather
than a fixed white: a theme is free to pick a light amber for
`.warning`, and white ink would wash out on it.
